purpose: Same-ELF launch-path-length calibration after R110-A control instruction count changed between series. Diagnose the instrument before any further runtime variant.
sampling: Eight fresh daemons, four paired comparisons with alternating order, identical c9ada3dc ELF at the two historical argv[0] lengths. Copy each launch into a unique owned temporary directory; verify /proc/PID/exe before and after. No source or ELF changes.
analysis: Only test reproducibility of a launch-path-size dependence. Report all instruction counts and hashes; no CPU acceptance or heap causality claim. If seen, normalize executable launch names in future cohorts and discard cross-cohort attribution.
decision: Either outcome stops further runtime edits until counter comparisons use the same launch-path length. Four pairs characterize a deterministic input confound, not a performance significance test.
boundaries: Enable ACK after warmup before the three clock reads; disable ACK after the loop and the three clock reads. No per-request instrumentation. Final callback validates delivery; bounded trailing daemon work can straddle the CPU-clock/disable boundary. Counts include this boundary overhead and are divided by 50000.
